newsitem.title: USA: Ethanol subsidy cleared by U.S. Senate tax panel.
newsitem.headline: Ethanol subsidy cleared by U.S. Senate tax panel.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Finance Committee Thursday approved an amendment to a sweeping tax reform measure that would extend tax incentives for ethanol producers but at the same time gradually reduce that subsidy over the next five years.
The amendment, which was approved by a vote of 16 in favor and only four against, was introduced by Iowa Republican Sen. Charles Grassley and Illinois Democrat Sen. Carol Moseley-Braun.
"We have a proposal here that is good for agriculture, good for national security...it's just good, good, good," Grassley said.
The measure would reduce the ethanol subsidy to 5.3 cents in 2001, to 5.2 cents in 2003 and 2004, and to 5.1 cents beyond that until 2007.
The current tax break for ethanol is 5.4 cents per gallon at the pump.
The Senate measure differs from a tax bill that passed the U.S. House Ways and Means Committee that does away with ethanol subsidies altogether.
The panel is due to vote later tonight on a sweeping tax package that includes $85 billion in tax cuts over the next five years.
